Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

there is phrase

also there are, there was, there were, is there, are there

classical

Hor. S. 1.1.106: est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs
Vulg. Jo. 6.9: Est puer ūnus hīc

est, sunt (first in the clause)

esse put first, the thing after it

there is, there are

Brings something new into view, as at the start of a story (est in Carpathiō Neptūnī gurgite vātēs, Verg. G. 4.387). Elsewhere Latin seldom frames a sentence this way: it prefers a verb that says what the thing does or where it is (jacet, stat, situs est) to an English “there was”.

Other words

  • nōn est quod (+ subjunctive) — there is no reason to

    phrase: est with quod and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Phaedr. 2.1.7: nōn est quod timeās

    Also nihil est quod (see “reason”), and sunt quī, there are those who (see “certain”).

  • ecquid (+ genitive) — is there any …?

    neuter of ecquis, with a partitive genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.8.1: quaerō ecquid litterārum

    See “someone” for ecquis.

Examples

  • Est puer ūnus hīc quī habet quīnque pānēs hordeāceōs et duōs piscēs: sed haec quid sunt inter tantōs?

    There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish: but what are they among so many?Vulg. Jo. 6.9

  • est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs

    there is a measure in things; there are, in short, fixed boundsHor. S. 1.1.106

  • sunt bona, sunt quaedam mediōcria, sunt mala plūra quae legis hīc: aliter nōn fit, Avīte, liber

    there are good things, there are some middling ones, and there are more bad ones that you read here: no other way is a book made, AvitusMart. 1.16.1–2

  • est in Carpathiō Neptūnī gurgite vātēs caeruleus Prōteus

    in Neptune’s Carpathian sea there is a seer, sea-blue ProteusVerg. G. 4.387–388

  • cui placidus ille: nōn est quod timeās, ait

    and to him the lion said calmly: “There’s nothing for you to fear”Phaedr. 2.1.7

  • vocō, quaerō ecquid litterārum. negant.

    I call them and ask whether there are any letters. They say no.Cic. Att. 2.8.1

See also reason, certain, someone, is it …?.
